was: MDWFP state park near Wesson on Lake Lincoln. 71 developed RV sites with concrete pads, concrete tables, grills, electric (sites 1-26 water/electric; 27-71 water/electric/sewer); two bathhouses, laundry, central dump station, swim beach. Reservable online up to 12 months ahead. 22 sites are lake-side. (Separate primitive walk-in sites are FCFS.)

was: MDWFP State Fishing Lake 5 mi west of Monticello on US-84 (Lawrence County). 20 camping pads with water/electric hookups, nature trail, two boat ramps with courtesy piers, restroom with showers, two handicapped fishing piers. FCFS - no reservation system; call the State Lake office. Lake was drained/renovated 2018 (new water-control structure, restocked) and reopened; fully operational as of 2025-2026.

was: MDWFP State Fishing Lake ~5 mi west of Collins (Covington County) on 79-acre Lake Mike Conner. Back-in RV sites with 30-amp electric and water (no sewer), dump station, boat ramps, pavilions, fishing. FCFS - no reservation system; call the State Lake office. Fishing permit/license required except free-fishing days.

was: MDWFP State Fishing Lake near Mize (Smith County), formerly Lake Ross Barnett, now officially Prentiss Walker Lake. Campground has pull-through and back-in RV sites with electric/water (some full hookups), 30/50-amp, dump station, boat launch, trails, restrooms/showers. FCFS - no reservation system; call the State Lake office. Known for large bluegill/redear. This is the Smith County state lake, NOT the Ross Barnett Reservoir near Jackson.

FCFS - no reservation system; call the State Lake office. Holds the state Channel Catfish record.

was: MDWFP state park. 16 RV sites on level concrete pads with 30/50-amp electric, water, sewer; fire rings, picnic tables, grills; bathhouse with hot showers and laundry; dump station. Alligator Lake shore fishing and kayaking; 18-hole disc golf. Reservable online or by phone; some sites held FCFS.

was: First-come-first-served NPS campground on the Natchez Trace Parkway (Milepost 193.1, atop Little Mountain), 18 drive-in sites (mix of pull-through and back-in), no hookups, flush toilets, drinking water, 14-day limit. Not on recreation.gov (FCFS). Note: may be temporarily closed for parkway road construction - verify before visiting. Rechecked 2026-09-30: closed since June 9, 2025 for construction; no reopening date (NPS). --Claude

was: NPS Natchez Trace Parkway campground at MP 54.8, 22 sites (mix of pull-through and back-in), no hookups, no showers, vault/restrooms. FCFS, no reservations (not on recreation.gov for booking). Accommodates large RVs - sites fit rigs to ~55 ft incl. tow. Water can be intermittent; come self-contained. 14-day stay limit. --Claude

was: USFS Tombigbee NF campground around Choctaw Lake. ~21 sites with water + 50-amp/electric hookups, picnic table, fire ring; flush toilets, showers, drinking water, dump station. No-wake lake with swim beach and fishing pier. Sites 1-12 FCFS, sites 13-21 reservable online. --Claude

was: USFS De Soto NF recreation area on the 240-acre Turkey Fork Reservoir. 20 RV sites with water + 50-amp electric, picnic tables, fire rings; 8 primitive tent sites; 3 bathhouses (flush toilets, showers), dump station, boat ramp, floating dock, two swim areas. RV sites (6 reservable online, rest FCFS); tent sites $7. --Claude

was: 22-site NF campground around a small spring-fed lake in the Homochitto NF. All sites have water + electric hookups; flush toilets, hot showers, RV dump station. Loop B sites are more level and better suited to larger RVs; sites fit a 23-ft rig. $13 with federal pass. FCFS — you must arrive in person to claim a site; even-numbered sites, the pavilion, and group site are reservable online but the standard campground is first-come, first-served.

was: 34-site NF campground on 50-acre Marathon Lake in the Bienville NF, ~15 mi SE of Forest, MS. Sites have water + 30/50-amp electric; 2 bath houses with warm showers, dump station, boat ramp, swim area, picnic shelters. Campendium reports rigs up to 38 ft have fit (a few sites run short) — fine for a 23-ft RV. $13 senior. FCFS — arrive in person to claim a site; group pavilions reservable by phone.

was: Pat Harrison Waterway District water park on Flint Creek Reservoir. ~152 developed RV camping spurs with 50/30-amp service, plus primitive sites, cabins and camphouses. Reservable by phone (campsites 601-928-3051; cabins 1-800-748-9403). RV Life: 4, $$.

was: County-run RV park at the Forrest County Multipurpose Center, beside the 16-acre Forrest County Lake. 147 full-hookup back-in sites (30/50-amp, water, sewer), concrete pads, paved drives; site lengths range ~25-70 ft. FCFS, honor-system drop box $25/night, no reservations; occasional event conflicts (carnival/horse show) a few times yearly. RV Life: 4, $$.

Unrated on RV Life but drive-in RV access, FHU and currently-operating status confirmed firsthand on the operator's own site. RV Life: 0 (unrated), $.

was: NPS Hot Springs National Park. 44 sites, all reservable online (no FCFS). Full hookups: each site has 30/50-amp electric, water, sewer, and paved parking; modern restrooms but no showers. Open year-round. Sites are back-in (not pull-through). Gulpha Creek runs along the campground. --Claude

was: NPS Buffalo National River, Lower District. Over 80 drive-in sites across Loops A-E plus walk-in tent and group sites. The only campground in the park with RV hookups: all drive-in sites have water + 30/50-amp electric (no sewer); dump station, showers, flush restrooms (seasonal). Max RV length varies by site from 21 ft up to 65 ft, so a 23-ft rig fits. Reservable online and FCFS; B Loop open in winter with reduced amenities. Operates roughly mid-March to mid-November. --Claude
